mainTopic: Baking without an עירובי תבשילין, how many dishes the עירוב needs, and immersion when יום טוב follows שבת
overview: The גמרא asks whether food baked or cooked on יום טוב for שבת without an עירובי תבשילין may be eaten. It tries several proofs that the food is forbidden: the silence of a ברייתא, a ברייתא that forbids food made through הערמה, and sources about tithing, immersing vessels and cooking on שבת. Each proof is rejected. רב אדא בר מתנה, רב אשי and רב נחמן בר יצחק each reject one of the first proofs, and the later ones fail because those cases are different. The question is never settled. Next, the גמרא shows that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר tells the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about two dishes differently from our משנה. רבא rules like our משנה and בית הלל: one cooked dish is enough. אביי adds that if the עירוב is eaten after you began kneading, you may finish. A new משנה then discusses immersing people and vessels when יום טוב falls right after שבת. The גמרא notes that everyone forbids immersing a vessel on שבת, and רבה begins to explain that this is a rabbinic גזרה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Inference from what the ברייתא did not say
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that if baking without an עירוב were permitted after the fact, the ברייתא should have said so.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it were so (that the food is allowed), let the ברייתא simply teach: 'If he went ahead and baked, it is permitted!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to prove that food baked without an עירובי תבשילין is forbidden. Its proof comes from what the earlier ברייתא left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא gave a workaround: transfer your flour to someone else so the baking is done for them. If the food were allowed even after baking improperly, the ברייתא could have just said 'if he baked, it is fine.' Since it did not say that, the גמרא infers that the food must be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it were so (if your view were correct)
Let it teach (the ברייתא should have said)
He went against the rule and baked
The 'mixing of cooked foods' made before יום טוב that allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת

phrases.english: And if it is so (that the food is permitted),
phrases.notes: Refers to the possibility that baking without an עירוב is permitted after the fact.

phrases.english: let it teach: 'If he transgressed and baked, it is permitted!'
phrases.notes: The ברייתא's silence is taken as evidence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous amud of the ברייתא that permits transferring one's flour to others. Here the גמרא draws an inference from that ברייתא's silence.
steps.raayaObject: That food baked without an עירובי תבשילין is forbidden after the fact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The silence of the previous ברייתא, which offered only the flour-transfer workaround and never said 'if he baked, it is permitted.'

steps.title: The ברייתא only teaches proper solutions
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה explains that the תנא teaches only permitted solutions. Baking without an עירוב is forbidden at the start, so it would not be listed as a solution, even if the food is allowed afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנה said: The תנא teaches a solution that is permitted. He does not teach a 'solution' that involves doing something forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנה rejects the proof from Step 1. He explains why the ברייתא would stay silent even if the food is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Baking without an עירוב is forbidden at the start (לכתחילה), even if the bread might be allowed afterward (בדיעבד). A ברייתא that is advising a person what to do would never suggest 'just break the rule.' So its silence proves nothing about whether the food is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A remedy or solution to a problem
Of permission (done in a permitted way)
Of prohibition (done in a forbidden way)

steps.confusionAlert: רב אדא is NOT saying the food is permitted. He is only saying this ברייתא cannot prove it is forbidden. The question is still open.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said:
The tanna teaches a remedy that is permitted,
a remedy through a prohibited act he does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה: תַּנָּא, תַּקַּנְתָּא דְהֶיתֵּרָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of Step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the proof from the ברייתא's silence.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the ברייתא would list every possible outcome. In fact it lists only permitted courses of action, so leaving out a forbidden act shows nothing about the after-the-fact status.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: the laws of the עירוב and of eating it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. Whoever made an עירובי תבשילין may bake, cook and insulate food. If he ate the עירוב before doing so, he and others may no longer prepare food for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Whoever made an עירובי תבשילין may bake, cook and insulate food. If he wants to eat his עירוב, he may. If he ate it before he baked or insulated, he may not bake, cook or insulate, not for himself and not for others. And others may not bake or cook for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second attempt to prove the food is forbidden by quoting a new ברייתא. This first part sets up the background, and the actual proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that the עירוב must still exist at the time of cooking. Once it is eaten, the permission to cook for שבת is gone. This sets the stage for the ברייתא's next line about someone who has no עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source brought as proof)
Insulates (wraps food to keep it warm)
He has permission (it is up to him)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who placed an eiruv tavshilin
may bake, cook and insulate,
and if he wants to eat his eiruv,
he has permission.
If he ate it before he baked
phrases.notes: That is, he ate it on יום טוב before preparing food for שבת.

phrases.english: or before he insulated,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יֹאפֶה וְלֹא יְבַשֵּׁל וְלֹא יַטְמִין,
phrases.english: he may not bake, nor cook, nor insulate,
neither for himself nor for others.
And others may not bake or cook for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁהִנִּיחַ עֵירוּבֵי תַבְשִׁילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 2 rejected the first proof, the גמרא begins a new proof from a different ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That food cooked for שבת without a valid עירוב is forbidden after the fact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about eating one's עירובי תבשילין. Its decisive clause comes in Step 4.

steps.title: Food made through trickery is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: without an עירוב one may still cook for יום טוב, and leftovers may be used on שבת. But if he used הערמה, the food is forbidden. The גמרא takes this as proof that improperly made food is forbidden after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: However, he may cook for יום טוב, and if food is left over, it is left over for שבת, as long as he does not use trickery. And if he used trickery, it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punch line of the proof. The ברייתא says that food cooked for שבת through הערמה is forbidden, so the גמרא concludes that food prepared for שבת without an עירוב is forbidden after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking a large pot 'for יום טוב' while really intending it for שבת gets around the need for an עירוב. The ברייתא forbids that food even after it was cooked. The גמרא reasons that if a trickster's food is forbidden, then the food of someone who openly baked for שבת without an עירוב should be forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: Uses trickery (pretends to cook for יום טוב while really cooking for שבת)

phrases.english: But he may cook for the Festival,
and if he left over, he has left it over for Shabbat,
provided that he does not use trickery.
And if he used trickery, it is forbidden!
phrases.notes: This is the line the proof depends on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 3 and delivers its decisive clause.
steps.raayaObject: Food cooked on יום טוב for שבת in a forbidden way may not be eaten.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that food made through הערמה is forbidden.

steps.title: Trickery is treated more strictly than open sinning
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the proof. The רבנן were stricter with הערמה than with a מזיד, so the ruling on trickery tells us nothing about someone who simply baked without an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: You are talking about הערמה? הערמה is different, because the רבנן were stricter with it than with an intentional sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects the proof from Step 4. He shows that the הערמה case cannot be compared to plain baking without an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who sins openly knows he did wrong and may stop, and others will not copy him. A trickster thinks he found a legal loophole, so he and others may keep doing it, and the practice of making an עירוב could be forgotten. That is why the רבנן penalized הערמה by forbidding the food, and that penalty may not apply to a plain מזיד.

keyTerms.meaning: Trickery, a legal loophole used to dodge a prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: It seems backwards that a trickster is punished more than an open sinner. The reason is that trickery looks permitted, so it is more likely to spread. The open sinner knows he is doing wrong.
steps.whatToRemember: So far, two proofs that food baked without an עירובי תבשילין is forbidden have been rejected. The ברייתא's silence proves nothing (רב אדא בר מתנה), and the ban on food made through הערמה is a special stringency (רב אשי). Step 6 gives a second rejection of the same הערמה proof, and the גמרא keeps searching for a proof in steps 7–12.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for a principle used throughout שס: the רבנן often treat a sneaky loophole more harshly than an open violation, because a loophole can wear down observance of the law itself.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
You are speaking of trickery?
Trickery is different,
for the Rabbis were more stringent with it than with an intentional sinner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הַעֲרָמָה קָא אָמְרַתְּ, שָׁאנֵי הַעֲרָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Steps 3 and 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the proof from the ברייתא about הערמה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof treats הערמה and an open מזיד as the same. In fact הערמה carries a special stricter penalty, so the ruling on it cannot be applied to a plain intentional sinner.

steps.title: The strict ברייתא follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the proof from the ברייתא in a second way. He says it follows חנניה's version of בית שמאי, who are strict about how an עירוב must be made. בית הלל, the accepted view, are more lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Whose view is this ברייתא? It is חנניה's, following בית שמאי. A ברייתא teaches that חנניה says: בית שמאי say you may not bake unless your עירוב was bread, you may not cook unless your עירוב was a cooked dish, and you may not insulate food unless hot food was already insulated before יום טוב. בית הלל say: you make an עירוב with one cooked dish, and it covers all your needs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives another reason the ברייתא from step 4 proves nothing. He says that ברייתא follows the strict opinion of בית שמאי, as reported by חנניה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי require a separate kind of עירוב for each activity: bread for baking, a cooked dish for cooking, and hot food already insulated for insulating. A view this strict about עירוב could also be strict after the fact. We follow בית הלל, who are lenient, so the ברייתא tells us nothing about the הלכה for us.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? Used to identify the author of a source
Insulating food to keep it hot
All his needs: baking, cooking and insulating

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rejections. רב אשי (step 5) said הערמה is a special stricter case. רב נחמן בר יצחק says the whole ברייתא follows בית שמאי, a view we do not hold.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because the הלכה follows בית הלל, a source that matches בית שמאי's strict approach cannot settle the question.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Whose view is this? It is Ḥananya's,
and it follows Beit Shammai.
phrases.notes: חנניה reports what בית שמאי held.

phrases.english: As a baraita teaches: Ḥananya says,
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹפִין אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עֵרֵב בְּפַת,
phrases.english: One may not bake unless he made the eiruv with bread,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְבַשְּׁלִין אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עֵרֵב בְּתַבְשִׁיל,
phrases.english: and one may not cook unless he made the eiruv with a cooked dish,
and one may not insulate food unless

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ חַמִּין טְמוּנִין מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: hot food was already insulated from the eve of the Festival.
And Beit Hillel say:
One makes the eiruv with one cooked dish,
and does all his needs with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַנִּי — חֲנַנְיָה הִיא, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent rejection of the proof from step 4, alongside רב אשי's rejection in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא about הערמה and eating the עירוב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא follows בית שמאי's strict view of עירוב, not the accepted view of בית הלל.

steps.title: Proof from tithing produce on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: if someone tithes his produce on שבת by mistake he may eat it, but if he did it on purpose he may not. This seems to show that what was done wrongly on purpose is forbidden after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: If someone tithes his produce on שבת, by mistake he may eat it; on purpose he may not eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof from a משנה about tithing on שבת. Doing it on purpose makes the food forbidden afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tithing on שבת is a rabbinic prohibition, like baking without an עירוב. If the רבנן forbid the food when someone tithed on purpose, maybe they also forbid food baked on purpose without an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: One who separates tithes from his produce

phrases.english: We learned: One who tithes his produce on Shabbat,
if by mistake, he may eat it;
if on purpose, he may not eat it.
phrases.notes: This is the line the proof relies on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a different source.
steps.raayaObject: That food prepared without an עירוב is forbidden after the fact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about tithing on שבת: done on purpose, the food may not be eaten.

steps.title: Tithing case is where he has other food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה is about someone who has other produce to eat, so forbidding this produce does not hurt him much. Someone without an עירוב might have nothing to eat, so the רבנן may be lenient with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case is needed where he has other produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the tithing proof. It says the משנה is talking about a person who has other food available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding the tithed produce is a small penalty when he has other food. Someone who baked without an עירוב may have no other food for שבת, so the רבנן might not fine him. The two cases are not the same.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (a specific case)

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he has other produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִית לֵיהּ פֵּירֵי אַחֲרִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the tithing משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The tithing case involves someone with other food, so the penalty is small. It cannot be compared to someone who would be left with nothing to eat.

steps.title: Proof from immersing vessels on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another source: if someone immerses his vessels on שבת by mistake he may use them, but on purpose he may not. This again suggests that something done wrongly on purpose is forbidden after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone immerses his vessels on שבת, by mistake he may use them; on purpose he may not use them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof about immersing vessels on שבת. The next step (step 10) answers this proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Immersing vessels on שבת is forbidden by the רבנן because it looks like fixing a vessel. If doing it on purpose forbids using the vessels, maybe baking on purpose without an עירוב forbids the food too.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, introducing a proof
One who immerses his vessels in a מקוה to purify them

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who immerses his vessels on Shabbat,
if by mistake, he may use them;
if on purpose, he may not use them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the tithing proof was rejected, the גמרא tries another parallel source.
steps.raayaObject: That food prepared without an עירוב is forbidden after the fact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The source about immersing vessels on שבת: done on purpose, the vessels may not be used.

steps.title: Rejecting the proof from immersing vessels
steps.stepSummary: The vessels case is about someone who has other vessels, or who can borrow some. So forbidding these vessels costs him little.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, that ruling is needed for a case where he has other vessels. Or else, he can simply borrow vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 9. It says the vessels case is a situation where being strict does not really hurt the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he immersed the vessels on purpose, he loses almost nothing by not using them. He has other vessels, or he can borrow some from a neighbor. Someone without an עירוב may have no food for שבת, so the רבנן might be lenient with him. This is the same kind of answer as step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case; the גמרא narrows a source to a specific situation

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he has other vessels.
Alternatively, it is possible by borrowing.
phrases.notes: He can borrow vessels from others, so he loses little.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִית לֵיהּ מָאנֵי אַחֲרִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from immersing vessels on שבת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The vessels case involves very little loss, unlike someone who may have nothing to eat on שבת

steps.title: Proof from cooking on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that someone who cooks on שבת by mistake may eat the food, but if he cooked on purpose he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one who cooks on שבת by mistake may eat it. If he did it on purpose, he may not eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another proof. Here, food cooked against the rules on purpose is forbidden after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking is a food case, so here the person may also be left without food. The ruling is still strict for a מזיד. So it seems the same should apply to someone who skipped the עירוב on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; it introduces a proof from a source

phrases.english: Come and hear: one who cooks on Shabbat,
if by mistake, he may eat it;
if on purpose, he may not eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 10 rejects the vessels proof, the גמרא brings a new one
steps.raayaObject: That food made against the rules on purpose is forbidden after the fact, even when it is food

steps.title: שבת prohibitions are different
steps.stepSummary: The proof fails because breaking שבת is a much more serious sin than cooking on יום טוב for the next day without an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The prohibition of שבת is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from cooking on שבת. With this, the search for a proof ends without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking שבת carries כרת and סקילה, so the רבנן were extra strict about it. Skipping an עירוב תבשילין is only a rabbinic matter. So the strict ruling about שבת tells us nothing about it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different; it cannot be compared

steps.whatToRemember: Every proof for the case of skipping the עירוב on purpose (steps 1–12) was rejected. The question stays open: we never find out whether such a person may eat what he cooked.

phrases.english: The prohibition of Shabbat is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from cooking on שבת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A Torah-level שבת prohibition is far more serious than the rabbinic rule of עירוב תבשילין

steps.title: Our משנה does not match a certain תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'בית שמאי say: two dishes' and remarks that our משנה goes against another תנא's version of the dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'בית שמאי say two cooked dishes.' Our משנה is not in line with this other תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. Its remark sets up the next step, where it will bring the other תנא's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, the whole dispute is about the number of dishes: בית שמאי say two and בית הלל say one. The גמרא signals that another source tells the dispute in a different way.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in line with this תנא

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: two cooked dishes.
Our mishnah is not in accordance with this tanna,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the finished question about skipping the עירוב, to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה presents the dispute differently from another תנא

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says both sides agree that two dishes are needed. They only argue about a fish with an egg on it: is it one dish or two?
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said that בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that two dishes are needed. What do they argue about? About a fish with an egg on it. בית שמאי say two real dishes are needed. בית הלל say this one dish counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind its remark in step 13. This version of the dispute is different from our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, בית הלל are fine with one dish. In this ברייתא, everyone requires two dishes. The only question is whether a fish with an egg on top already counts as two. בית הלל say it does, and בית שמאי say it is only one.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who gives a different version of the dispute
A fish with an egg on it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In our משנה, בית הלל require only one dish. In this ברייתא, everyone requires two, and בית הלל simply count a fish with an egg on it as two.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:
Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel agree
that two dishes are needed.
About what did they argue?
About a fish with the egg on it,
for Beit Shammai say: two dishes are needed;
phrases.notes: In their view, the fish with an egg counts as only one dish.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: this one dish is enough.
phrases.notes: In their view, this one dish counts as two.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source mentioned in step 13
steps.raayaObject: That another תנא tells the dispute differently from our משנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר

steps.title: Both agree when the egg or leeks are mixed into the fish
steps.stepSummary: Both sides agree that if a sliced egg or mashed leeks are put inside the fish, it counts as two dishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that if he sliced an egg and put it into the fish, or mashed leeks and put them into the fish, these count as two dishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a case where even בית שמאי agree it is two dishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An egg simply sitting on the fish may be seen as part of one dish. Once the egg is sliced, or the leeks are mashed, and put into the fish, it becomes a second food that was really prepared. So everyone counts it as two.

phrases.english: And they agree that if he sliced an egg
and put it into the fish,
or if he mashed leeks
and put them into the fish,
that they are two dishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sliced egg or mashed leeks put inside the fish count as two dishes, according to everyone

steps.title: רבא rules like our משנה and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the הלכה follows the version in our משנה, according to בית הלל. One dish is enough for an עירוב תבשילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the הלכה follows the תנא of our משנה, according to בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final practical ruling on this dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא picks our משנה's version over רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version. Within that version he follows בית הלל. So a single cooked dish is enough for the עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the ruling here
Our תנא; the תנא of our משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows our משנה and בית הלל: one cooked dish is enough for an עירוב תבשילין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule for making an עירוב תבשילין: one cooked dish is enough.

phrases.english: Rava said: The halakha is like our tanna,
and according to Beit Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two versions of the dispute shown in steps 13–15
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Follow our משנה according to בית הלל: one dish is enough for an עירוב תבשילין

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: The עירוב Was Eaten or Lost
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that if the עירוב was eaten or lost, one may not cook relying on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If he ate it, or it got lost, he may not cook relying on it, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. This sets up אביי's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's basic rule is that the עירוב must still exist when you cook for שבת. If it is gone before you start, you have no permission to cook. The open question is what happens if it disappears in the middle.

keyTerms.meaning: He may not cook relying on it

phrases.english: If he ate it or it got lost —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יְבַשֵּׁל עָלָיו וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: he may not cook relying on it, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the debate about how many dishes are needed to a new line of the משנה about a lost עירוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the עירוב is gone, one may not start cooking for שבת on the basis of it.

steps.title: אביי: If You Already Started, You May Finish
steps.stepSummary: אביי teaches that if someone began kneading his dough while the עירוב existed, and then the עירוב was eaten, he may finish.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition: if a person started working on his dough, and then his עירוב was eaten, he may finish.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי limits the משנה's rule. The ban applies only to starting new cooking, not to finishing a job already begun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids cooking once the עירוב is gone. אביי explains that this only blocks a new start. Work that began while the עירוב was still valid may be completed, because it started in a permitted way.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold, we have a tradition

steps.whatToRemember: An עירוב תבשילין must exist when you start cooking for שבת. If it is eaten after you began, you may still finish that job.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule: losing the עירוב in the middle does not cancel cooking that has already begun.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We have a tradition,
if he began his dough
and his eiruv was eaten — he finishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of the משנה's ban that was just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who started baking with a valid עירוב may finish, even if the עירוב was eaten in the middle.

steps.title: New משנה: Immersing When יום טוב Falls on Sunday
steps.stepSummary: When יום טוב falls right after שבת, בית שמאי say everything must be immersed before שבת. בית הלל say כלים before שבת, but a person may immerse on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If יום טוב falls right after שבת, בית שמאי say: we immerse everything before שבת. בית הלל say: כלים before שבת, and a person on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks when people and כלים may be immersed so they are טהור for a יום טוב that comes right after שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People want to be טהור as soon as יום טוב begins, on מוצאי שבת, so the immersion has to happen on שבת or earlier. בית שמאי forbid any immersion on שבת. בית הלל allow a person to immerse on שבת but still forbid immersing כלים on שבת.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If it (the Festival) falls after Shabbat —
Beit Shammai say:
We immerse everything before Shabbat.
And Beit Hillel say:
Vessels before Shabbat,
and a person on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, טבילה before יום טוב, after the עירוב תבשילין discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, a person may immerse on שבת, but כלים must be immersed before שבת.

steps.title: What Both Sides Agree On
steps.stepSummary: Both sides agree that impure water may be purified by touching it to מקוה water while it sits in a stone vessel, but it may not be immersed. They also allow immersing on יום טוב 'from גב to גב and from חבורה to חבורה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Both agree that we may touch impure water to the מקוה, inside a stone vessel, to make it טהור, but we may not immerse it. And we may immerse from one level to another, and from one group to another.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists cases where בית שמאי and בית הלל agree. The גמרא will explain these cases later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stone vessel cannot become טמא, so it does not need its own immersion. Touching the water inside it to the מקוה (השקה) purifies the water without immersing a כלי. Real immersion, such as dipping the water in a vessel that is itself טמא, is not allowed, because that would also immerse the כלי. The last clause allows certain immersions on יום טוב, such as moving to a higher level of purity or switching to a different group eating the קרבן פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: We let it touch (bring water into contact with the מקוה)
A stone vessel, which cannot become טמא
From one level (of purity) to another
From one group (of קרבן פסח eaters) to another

steps.confusionAlert: השקה (touching) is not the same as טבילה (immersing). The water is purified by contact with the מקוה, so no כלי is being immersed.

phrases.english: And they agree that we bring the water into contact
in a stone vessel, to purify it,
but we do not immerse.
And we immerse from one level to another
and from one group to another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with points of agreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Purifying water through השקה in a stone vessel is allowed, but immersing it is not. Immersing from גב to גב and from חבורה to חבורה is allowed.

steps.title: Everyone Agrees: No Immersing Vessels on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that both sides of the משנה agree that a כלי may not be immersed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: In any case, everyone agrees that a כלי may not be immersed on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a point of agreement out of the משנה. This sets up the question of why the rule exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי forbid all immersion on שבת, and even בית הלל require כלים to be done before שבת. So immersing a כלי on שבת is forbidden according to everyone. The rule is clear, but its reason is not.

phrases.english: GEMARA: According to everyone, in any case —
a vessel on Shabbat, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes an inference from the משנה's dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both בית שמאי and בית הלל forbid immersing a כלי on שבת.

steps.title: Why Is Immersing a Vessel on Shabbat Forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ban on immersing a כלי on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why immersing a כלי on שבת is forbidden. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Immersing an object does not look like one of the forbidden מלאכות. So the גמרא wants to know the source of the ban.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes immersing a כלי on שבת forbidden?

steps.title: רבה: It Is a Rabbinic Decree
steps.stepSummary: רבה begins to answer that the ban is a גזרה, a protective decree of the Sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה starts his answer: the ban is a rabbinic גזרה. The details of the decree continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling it a גזרה means that immersing a כלי is not itself a Torah-level מלאכה. The Sages forbade it to protect against a real שבת violation. The next lines will say which one.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree made by the Sages

steps.confusionAlert: The text stops in the middle of רבה's answer. What the decree guards against is explained right on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabba said: It is a decree

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question just asked.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban is a rabbinic גזרה. The details continue on the next amud.
